raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload: false`, DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables live in HBM, but every lookup still goes through DP collectives: a pynccl `all_gather` of the hash ids and an `all_to_all_single` of the rows on the node-local `edp` group. Decode runs in FULL CUDA graphs, which do not honor `eager_break_during_capture`, so these collectives are captured next to MegaMoE's cross-rank kernels. In DEP decode on GB200, every rank then blocks in `graph.replay()` of the same decode graph at the first real step (seen with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`); host-offloaded tables, with no NCCL in the graph, never hang. I did not pin down the exact NCCL/MegaMoE interaction. This PR removes the collectives instead: GPU tables are row-sharded over the Engram DP group in symmetric memory, and each rank looks up only its own tokens, reading every row from the owning peer's HBM. Lookups need no collective, barrier or graph break.

* **Kernel.** `_engram_lookup_kernel` gains `PEER_ROWS`. With it, `weight` is a per-rank pointer table: a row's owner is `id // PEER_ROWS`, and its scales follow the rows in the same symmetric buffer. Tables are read-only after loading, so reads need no synchronization.
* **When.** `cpu_offload: false`, TP=1 and an Engram DP group (co-located DP replicas). The table sets `dp_size = 1`, as `dp_shared_memory` does, and `DeepseekV4Model` reads that to skip the hash gather and dummy hashes. Host tables keep `dp_shared_memory` / `EngramPeerExchange`, since symmetric memory cannot map another process's host memory.
* **Across nodes.** By default the group stays node-local. With `embedding_across_dp: true` (off by default), GPU tables are split over every DP rank, e.g. 1/32 of the table per GPU at DEP32; all DP ranks must then share one NVLink domain, as on GB200 NVL72. A group with the DP group's ranks reuses `_DP` instead of building a second communicator: a separate 32-rank group cost ~1.1 GiB/GPU and failed `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`.
* **Not covered.** GPU tables with TP > 1 keep head sharding and its collectives. Peer mode stages BF16 rows per layer rather than `EngramBatch`'s packed MXFP8 rows, so `wkv` quantizes its own input; feeding packed peer rows to `EngramBatch` is a possible follow-up.

## Where it matters

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode-only on GB200, DEP16 / DEP32 (DP x TP1 + EP), 16 requests/rank, MegaMoE, MegaAttention, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance 3.51), EPLB, full decode CUDA graphs, `DecodeBenchConnector` replaying an agentic coding trace. Unprofiled steady state (+60 to +240 s), one run each, on a development tree based on `fe4df3df` with #61767; its Engram code is identical to main. Without this PR, `cpu_offload: false` hangs in this setup, so the baseline is the default host offload. GPU tables use `embedding_across_dp: true`.

| | host offload | GPU tables, peer read |
| -- | --: | --: |
| DEP16 step (ms) | 14.13 | 13.71 |
| DEP16 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,777 | 3,827 |
| DEP32 step (ms) | 13.15 | 12.90 |
| DEP32 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,877 | 3,939 |
| Model memory, DEP16 / DEP32 (GiB/GPU) | | 28.9 / 20.3 |

## Microbenchmark

Both Engram layers' lookups for one decode step, 96 tokens/rank, 16 ranks on 4 GB200 nodes, CUDA graph replay with fresh ids, median over ranks.

| Table layout | us/step |
| -- | --: |
| Host UVA (offload) | 233-324 |
| HBM, heads over 4 GPUs + `all_gather` + `all_to_all` (main; hangs in FULL graphs) | 46.7 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs + `all_gather` + `reduce_scatter` | 180.6 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs, peer read (this PR) | 19.8 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
```

* `test_engram_table_shared_across_dp_replicas` (4 GPUs): the TP1 x DP4 GPU-table case now takes the peer path, asserts that no DP `all_gather` runs, and replays a FULL CUDA graph with fresh ids.
* `test_engram_group_creation_honors_model_and_options`: TP1 x DP4 cases for the node-local group vs `embedding_across_dp`, and `_DP` reuse.

## Test Result

On 4 x GB200: 29 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaAttention, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`.

| | Engram tables | strict match | flexible extract |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| this PR, DEP8 over two GB200 nodes | GPU, rows over all 8 DP ranks (peer read) | 92.57% (±0.72) | 92.72% |
| #61371, DEP4 | host offload | 92.87% (±0.71) | |

The first revision of this PR gave 92.87% / 92.95% on the same setup.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# head node
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --port 8123 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-address <head> --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false,"embedding_across_dp":true}' \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --numa-bind
# second node: the same command plus --headless --data-parallel-start-rank 4

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8123/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `engram symmetric memory`, `engram peer`, `engram cpu_offload`, `engram hang` and `engram DP`. #59923 and #56512 cover the exchange for host-offloaded tables; #60625 changes head sharding for TP16/TP32 and keeps the collectives.
